name: Chaozhou Assembly Hall
kicker: Chaozhou hall for the sea gods
summary: The Chaozhou merchants’ hall at 157 Nguyễn Duy Hiệu, built in 1845 for the gods of wind and wave who kept the port’s voyages safe. The draw is the carving: a wooden frame of folk-story motifs and reliefs built up in porcelain. A short stop, quieter than the dragon court on Trần Phú.
fee: 20,000 VND from 10 Aug 2026, or a combination ticket
heroCaption: The hall front, with the incense burner in the court

notice.title: The sea-god hall
notice.body: This is the hall for the gods of wind and wave, a walk beyond the Trần Phú core. Door hours are not published, so come in the morning.

body: The hall is at 157 Nguyễn Duy Hiệu. Chaozhou merchants built it in 1845 as their meeting place and their own place of worship, and people also call it chùa Âm Bổn. The gods here govern wind and wave, so that voyages out of the port would go smoothly.

The building is a carved wooden frame, with motifs from folk stories and reliefs built up in porcelain. Come in the morning. If your ticket includes one assembly hall, the Fujian hall is the long one and the Cantonese hall is the dragon court. This is the sea-god hall.

figures.caption: The gate on Nguyễn Duy Hiệu
figures.alt: The red and green gate of the Chaozhou Assembly Hall in Hoi An, with lanterns

gettingThere: Walk to 157 Nguyễn Duy Hiệu, beyond the Trần Phú core.
admissionNote: No separate price for this building. From 10 Aug 2026: 20,000 VND per person per building, the same for every visitor (Da Nang Resolution 98/2026). Heritage centre notices of 26 Jan and 16 Mar 2026: 80,000 VND (streetscape, Chùa Cầu or Miếu Quan Công, and two other works) or 120,000 VND (adds a museum and three other works), usable through a stay of up to three days. A May 2026 article counts those as four and six works. Ask at the booth which ticket is on sale.
